     1	# Proposal
     2	
     3	<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
     4	     Revised 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A2. -->
     5	
     6	## Why
     7	
     8	Users need to retrieve relevant synced discourse nodes from their agent interface without opening Roam or Obsidian during retrieval or installing a platform-specific MCP for each. This v0 makes that collection available through a local MCP and a documented direct API, using a space account session handed over by the plugin.
     9	
    10	## What Changes
    11	
    12	- Provide four read-only operations through both interfaces: get a node, search nodes, discover node types, and get discourse context. The MCP is local: users install it, and the agent client launches it on their machine. Validate setup and these operations in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is not supported in v0.
    13	- The plugin hands the agent its own session for the space account, as specified in `mcp-session-access`. The agent acts as the space (Option A2): the session keeps the space account's read access, and the database refuses writes made with it. The MCP's tools and the API's operations also expose only retrieval.
    14	- Retrieve every synced discourse node readable by the space account, including accessible shared nodes that have never been imported into the client. Permissions follow current access: new access becomes available and removed access stops working. Signing out a handed-over session stops it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds stay valid until they expire.
    15	- Use per-space sessions as the v0 identity model. Access to another space's synced but unpublished nodes requires a bundle from that space. This does not promise one credential representing a person's combined access across spaces.
    16	- Return node ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link when fetching a node. Attachment downloads and image/file contents are excluded.
    17	- Reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. V0 does not require title-only re-embedding. Hybrid search, including keyword indexing and reciprocal rank fusion, is deferred to a later release. Return node ID, title, type, short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance.
    18	- Default search to 10 results, allow at most 30, and omit pagination. Apply no relevance cutoff in v0: weak matches may be returned. Empty results mean no eligible searchable nodes under the access and filter constraints, not a judgment that nothing is relevant.
    19	- Discover types present on currently readable nodes. Accept an optional filter of one or more type IDs, matching any selected type; omission searches all types. Further search-scope toggles and filters are deferred.
    20	- Return discourse context as incoming and outgoing one-hop explicit discourse relationships, including relationship type/direction and connected-node ID, title, and type. Return only relationships with two readable endpoints; retrieve connected bodies separately. Ordinary backlinks are excluded.
    21	
    22	### Boundaries and known limitations
    23	
    24	- Retrieval reads already-synced data. Candidate-node ingestion/retrieval, general non-discourse content, canvas functions, write-back, relation creation, candidate elevation, feedback capture, arbitrary-depth server traversal, and imported-only filtering are outside v0. Agents may repeat one-hop calls.
    25	- Accessible but unimported results may feel unfamiliar or outside the user's working collection. Results must not imply local import membership. Tracking that membership is not a v0 dependency. Semantic coverage follows the existing embedding inputs, which differ by platform and node representation; information absent from those inputs does not directly contribute to matching. Real-query evaluation examples and relevance thresholds are deferred.
    26	- A separate agent principal (Option B), a hosted MCP, and ChatGPT support are outside v0. Signing out a session takes effect when its current access token expires, not immediately.
    27	
    28	## Capabilities
    29	
    30	### New Capabilities
    31	
    32	- `agent-read-access`: Plugin-initiated session handoff, the space account as principal and its current read access, and database-enforced read-only access for handed-over sessions.
    33	- `discourse-retrieval`: Node payloads, semantic search using existing embeddings, readable-type discovery/filtering, and authorized one-hop discourse context.
    34	- `headless-retrieval-api`: Documented direct access to the four operations using the space account session and shared retrieval/access rules.
    35	- `discourse-mcp`: Local MCP delivery of the same operations, validated in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex.
    36	
    37	### Modified Capabilities
    38	
    39	- None; the repository currently has no existing OpenSpec capability specs.
    40	
    41	## Impact
    42	
    43	Expected affected areas are the narrow retrieval RPCs and integration with existing semantic search in `packages/database`, a new local MCP package, the connect command in `apps/roam` and `apps/obsidian` (through `mcp-session-access`), and `apps/website` as the host of the direct API routes and the query embedding route. This change depends on `mcp-session-access`, specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff` and not yet in this repository. It also depends on the shared CrossApp contracts in `packages/database`: `DbCrossAppNode`, the `dbNodeToCrossApp` converter (ENG-1985) and the `{ nodes, spaces }` listing envelope (ENG-2091). Node payloads use these contracts, and the `rid` is the node ID (design.md, Decision 5). Read-only is enforced by a read-only database role that a Supabase access token hook assigns to handed-over sessions, so `packages/database` also gains that role and hook. ENG-2057's feasibility evaluation of read-only delegation is input to it. The separate agent-access experiment is a design input, not evidence of deployed behavior or approval of its broader storage-read scope.
    44	
    45	### Open decisions and dependencies
    46	
    47	- **All hands (resolved 2026-11-10):** a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity. The per-space baseline stands; whether one agent should span several spaces is open.
    48	- **Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 notes record option A2. The spec owner chose A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording. See design.md, Decision 4.
    49	- **Node representation:** reusing `CrossAppNode` and `rid` for the agent API is pending Michael's confirmation.
    50	- **Design:** Credential-bearing MCP URLs are removed. The direct API is thin hosted routes in `apps/website` (design.md, Decision 1). Existing embeddings are retained; the retrieval query must add access/type filtering and limits without the existing semantic function's relevance threshold. No broader read-auditing project is implied.
    51	- **Validation:** Requirements and scenarios are captured in the capability specs. Implementation tasks are in tasks.md, grouped by proposed ticket; a small real-query relevance evaluation set remains to be developed; no numerical relevance or latency target has been agreed.
    52	- Scope reflects the supplied September 15 meeting research brief, the 2026-09-25 exploration, and the 2026-11-10 decisions. Historical July aspirations do not expand v0.
=== changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/design.md
     1	# Design
     2	
     3	<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
     4	     Revised 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A2. -->
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	See proposal.md for motivation and the four capability specs for the behavior contract. This design follows the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity (see Decision 4). It depends on the `mcp-session-access` handoff specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`, which is not yet in this repository.
     9	
    10	The checkout has useful pieces, but no implemented agent-grant layer was found:
    11	
    12	- Both client admin panels create a 45-second handoff through `create_secret_token` and open `/auth/token` with `/auth/group` as the destination. The website establishes a cookie session. `secret_tokens.sql` supports one-time consumption.
    13	- `Concept` represents node instances, schemas, and materialized relationships. `Content` joins by `(space_id, source_local_id)` and has multiple variants. The `my_*` views and access helpers already express space and resource-level readability.
    14	- `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimensional `text-embedding-3-small` vectors and ranks by cosine distance. Its existing general search RPC has a relevance threshold and no discourse-type predicate. The Roam search experiment subsequently looks up titles and filters locally; that cannot serve headless retrieval.
    15	- Obsidian embeds `direct` title content. Roam also embeds `direct_and_description` for some nodes. Preserve these existing vectors and inputs, as agreed; no title-only re-embedding migration is required.
    16	- Full content is synced separately. Roam converts it into a cross-app representation; Obsidian stores markdown. Missing full content and missing embeddings are distinct states.
    17	- `apps/website/app/api/embeddings/openai/small/route.ts` embeds text with the team's OpenAI key. It has no authentication: it applies CORS only, which non-browser callers ignore.
    18	- On `origin/main` (2026-11-11), ENG-1985 added `dbNodeToCrossApp` and `dbNodesToCrossApp`, and ENG-2091 made discovery return `DbCrossAppNode` in a `SharedNodeListing`. The other facts in this list were read from an older checkout of `main`.
    19	- Most row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role; four target `authenticated`. No custom access token hook is configured (it is commented out in `packages/database/supabase/config.toml`).
    20	
    21	## Goals / Non-Goals
    22	
    23	**Goals:** Reuse existing data, vectors, and access semantics; expose only read operations to agents; keep the MCP and the direct API on the same retrieval semantics; expose sync gaps without silently substituting incomplete content.
    24	
    25	**Non-Goals:** A new personal identity system, copied permission snapshots, a second embedding pipeline, hybrid ranking, attachment/storage APIs, or a general-purpose database proxy. A separate agent principal (Option B) and a hosted MCP are out of v0. The database package owns SQL/contracts; the website owns the API routes and the local MCP owns its transport.
    26	
    27	## Decisions
    28	
    29	### 1. A local MCP that calls the database directly
    30	
    31	The MCP is a local stdio server that the user installs and the agent client launches on the user's machine. It connects to Supabase with the handed-over space account session and calls the narrow retrieval RPCs directly. No DG-hosted layer sits between the MCP and the database, and no DG-hosted MCP endpoint exists in v0.
    32	
    33	```
    34	Roam / Obsidian --> connect command --> session bundle (shown once)
    35	                                               |
    36	                                 local MCP config on the user's machine
    37	                                               |
    38	agent client --stdio--> local MCP --+--> Supabase retrieval RPCs (as the space account)
    39	                                    |
    40	                                    +--> website embedding route (search queries only)
    41	
    42	developer --HTTPS + bearer token--> apps/website API routes --> same retrieval RPCs
    43	```
    44	
    45	The retrieval RPCs are the shared core. Each MCP tool validates its inputs, calls one RPC, and returns structured results plus a compact text representation. All tools are marked read-only.
    46	
    47	The RPCs are a contract with every installed copy of the MCP, and those copies cannot be force-updated. Change an RPC's signature only by adding a new version alongside the old one.
    48	
    49	**Direct API.** A developer-facing API for callers not using MCP is a set of thin routes in `apps/website` (`headless-retrieval-api`). Each route authenticates the caller's bearer access token against Supabase, embeds search queries on the server, and calls the same retrieval RPCs as the space account, so row-level security applies. The routes hold no credential between requests. The MCP does not depend on them.
    50	
    51	**Alternative for the API:** documenting the retrieval RPCs themselves as the API needs no hosting, but makes the database schema a public contract, returns raw Postgres errors, and leaves callers to embed queries through the unauthenticated route.
    52	
    53	**Alternatives:** A hosted remote MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 design) reaches ChatGPT and needs no install, but requires a hosted credential transport. It was rejected on 2026-11-10 in favour of a local MCP, given the constraint to write to the platform later and target users who already work in agentic harnesses. Routing the local MCP through a hosted API was also considered: it would absorb RPC changes, but adds no security, because the database already refuses writes made with the MCP's session (Decision 4).
    54	
    55	### 2. Hand the MCP its own space account session
    56	
    57	The credential is a Supabase session for the space account, opened by the plugin and handed over as a bundle: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and refresh token. `mcp-session-access` specifies the handoff, the session registry, and sign-out. The plugin keeps no copy and shows the bundle once. The MCP persists each rotated refresh token and runs as a single instance per bundle. The session's registry row is what makes it read-only (Decision 4).
    58	
    59	**Alternative (superseded 2026-11-10):** The 2026-09-25 design provisioned a separate Supabase auth user per agent grant, issued an opaque final credential through a website management session, and stored the agent's login secret server-side. That needs a hosted server and a separate principal, and A2 has neither.
    60	
    61	### 3. ~~Proposed MCP connection uses a credential-bearing URL~~ — removed
    62	
    63	Removed 2026-11-10. It existed to carry a credential to a hosted MCP through clients that cannot send custom headers. A local MCP reads the bundle from its own configuration. The client/redaction release gate and the OAuth alternative are removed with it.
    64	
    65	### 4. The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions (Option A2)
    66	
    67	Decided 2026-11-10: the MCP acts as the space account, and the database refuses writes made with its session. `mcp-session-access` records each handed-over session in `mcp_session`. A Supabase custom access token hook runs whenever a token is issued or refreshed. When the token's session is in `mcp_session`, the hook sets the JWT `role` claim to a read-only database role, `mcp_reader` (name proposed), instead of `authenticated`. Plugin sessions keep `authenticated`.
    68	
    69	`mcp_reader` has `SELECT` on the tables retrieval reads, and `EXECUTE` on the retrieval RPCs and the access helpers they call. It has no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, and no `EXECUTE` on sync, upsert or `create_secret_token`. Row-level security still applies: policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, and the four `TO authenticated` policies need review. Reads therefore follow the space account's current access with no grant layer.
    70	
    71	The MCP's tools and the API's operations still expose only retrieval, but they are no longer what enforces read-only.
    72	
    73	**Revocation is delayed.** The hook runs at issue and refresh, so a signed-out session keeps its current access token until `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this over B's immediate revocation.
    74	
    75	**Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product notes record "option A2" (Roam block `guIcK3Z9M`) and name the threat as overeager agentic harnesses that bypass the MCP's guards. A tool-layer gate is that kind of guard; a database role is not. The spec owner chose plain A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording.
    76	
    77	**Alternatives:** (A) the same session with the space account's full permissions and read-only only at the tool layer. It is about a week less work, but any process holding the bundle can write to the space. (B) a separate, permanently read-only agent principal with an `agent_reader` role and a grant table, the 2026-09-25 version of this decision. It revokes immediately, but the 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for about twice A2's extra work.
    78	
    79	### 5. Represent nodes as CrossApp nodes
    80	
    81	**Changed 2026-11-13: the node identifier is now the node's `rid`, not `Concept.id`, to match Sid's `shared-node-discovery` spec ([PR #1570](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1570)), in which discovery returns each node as a `CrossAppNode`.** ENG-1985 and ENG-2091 implemented that on 2026-11-11: `dbNodesToCrossApp` in `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts database rows to `DbCrossAppNode` (a `CrossAppNode` with `rid` and `modifiedAt` required), and discovery returns a `SharedNodeListing` of `{ nodes, spaces }`. Retrieval uses the same converter, so an agent and the plugins see the same node under the same ID.
    82	
    83	**IDs.** A node's ID is its `rid`: its space's URI followed by its `localId` (a Roam block uid, an Obsidian file's ID). A type's ID is the node's `nodeType`: the type's `localId` within the node's space, or the type's `rid` when it belongs to another space. Identically named types in different spaces stay separate. Look a node up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
    84	
    85	**Payload.** Return each node as a `DbCrossAppNode`, inside an envelope that follows discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` pattern: the spaces map gives each node's space name, URI and platform, and type labels come from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`. Search adds a score and an excerpt per node. Do not define a separate node type for agents.
    86	
    87	**Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`; `coreTitle` is the title without the type's format. The converter leaves out `content.full`, as discovery does, so get-node fetches the full Content separately, as node import does, and returns stored text/markdown, not rendered HTML. Preserve source links as text; do not fetch referenced assets or mint storage download URLs. Provenance comes from the `rid` and the spaces map. A source link refers to the origin and never claims the node exists in the caller's vault.
    88	
    89	**Gaps are errors.** `dbNodesToCrossApp` skips any row it cannot convert (missing direct content, author or node type) and logs a warning. Listings and search may skip such rows, as discovery does. Get-node for one ID must not: it converts the row with `dbNodeToCrossApp` and maps the failure to an explicit code, so a node that doesn't exist or isn't readable returns `not_found` and a node lacking its full Content returns `content_unavailable`. Distinguish a stored empty body from a missing row. Fixture validation must exercise these states for both platforms before release.
    90	
    91	**Type discovery** derives distinct types from readable node instances, independently of embeddings, with labels from the readable schemas. Missing schema data is a sync/access-integrity error, not a reason to bypass permissions.
    92	
    93	**Alternatives:** `Concept.id` serialized as a decimal string (the previous version of this decision) is a database-internal ID that no plugin uses; it would give the same node a second identity. An agent-specific node payload would rebuild, from the same rows, the second node representation that ENG-2091 just removed. Content IDs as node IDs would expose content variants as duplicate nodes.
    94	
    95	### 6. Reuse semantic vectors with a retrieval-specific query
    96	
    97	Embed each search query with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions to match the existing table. A local MCP has no server and no provider key, so it embeds through the existing website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small` and passes the vector to the search RPC. That route is unauthenticated today; see Risks. The API's search route embeds on the server after authenticating the caller. A caller-supplied vector cannot widen access, because the RPC ranks only nodes readable by the caller.
    98	
    99	Add a dedicated read-only search RPC using the existing embedding table and cosine-distance ordering. Keep existing RPC behavior for current consumers. In this query:
   100	
   101	- Resolve readable discourse node instances and any selected schema IDs.
   102	- Join their current non-obsolete, usable embeddings for existing `direct` and `direct_and_description` content. Preserve the stored input semantics, including descriptions.
   103	- Where multiple eligible embeddings represent one node, use its best similarity and return it once.
   104	- Sort by similarity descending and node ID as a stable tie-breaker, then apply the requested limit. Authorization, type filtering, and deduplication occur before the limit.
   105	
   106	Do not copy the current threshold predicate or the Roam experiment's post-limit local filtering. Do not replace the threshold with zero, since negative similarities remain eligible. Do not add keyword indexes, hybrid fusion, or collection re-embedding.
   107	
   108	Nodes without a current usable embedding are absent from search but remain eligible for get-node/type discovery/context. Embedding-provider failures are errors, not empty results. Create excerpts from the first 300 Unicode code points of available synced body text, with a fallback to the stored semantic input when full content is absent; excerpts are not evidence that the query matched the body. Both interfaces document this behavior.
   109	
   110	**Alternative:** Calling the existing threshold RPC unchanged violates the agreed no-cutoff behavior and can lose results when type filtering follows its limit. A dedicated query reuses the existing search mechanism while preserving current consumers.
   111	
   112	### 7. Resolve discourse context using named roles
   113	
   114	Find readable materialized relation instances connected to the requested node, explicitly filtering `is_relation` and excluding schemas. Use `reference_content` source/destination roles to determine direction; the derived `refs` array identifies candidates but does not encode direction and can include other references. Require the relation, relationship type metadata, and both endpoints to be readable before returning a relationship summary.
   115	
   116	Return each relation ID with its type, direction, and connected-node summary. Preserve separate materialized relationships rather than deduplicating by labels. A self-link can produce both incoming and outgoing entries. Do not traverse beyond the requested node's incident relationships or expand ordinary backlinks.
   117	
   118	Return complete one-hop results within the host's response budget. If the result cannot fit, return an explicit `result_too_large` error rather than silently truncate or add an undocumented pagination contract. Full node bodies use the same complete-or-error policy. A proposed 1 MiB serialized response budget is an implementation guardrail to validate against Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, not a relevance or latency target.
   119	
   120	**Alternative:** Expanding every ID in `refs` would expose non-discourse references and lose direction. Silent truncation would make incomplete discourse context appear complete.
   121	
   122	### 8. API contract and operational behavior
   123	
   124	Direct API routes and the corresponding MCP tools:
   125	
   126	| Direct API | MCP tool | Inputs |
   127	| --- | --- | --- |
   128	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | Node `rid` |
   129	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | Query, optional type IDs, optional limit |
   130	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | None |
   131	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | Node `rid` |
   132	
   133	Node IDs are `rid`s (Decision 5). They contain `/` and `:`, so the API takes them URL-encoded in the path.
   134	
   135	Use shared Zod input/output schemas and generate or check the tool and API documentation against them. Reject blank queries, malformed `rid`s, empty explicitly supplied type filters, and non-integer/out-of-range limits with `invalid_request`. Omitted limits default to 10; valid limits are 1-30. Unknown but syntactically valid type IDs simply match no nodes. Results carry a request ID and `data` or an error object with a stable code and safe message.
   136	
   137	Missing, expired, or signed-out sessions fail authentication. Use the same `not_found` for nonexistent and unreadable nodes, `content_unavailable` for a readable node with missing required synced content, and `result_too_large` for response-budget failures; database and embedding failures are dependency errors. Return these as MCP tool errors with the same codes rather than serializing exceptions; the API maps them to 401, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Do not turn failed queries into successful empty collections.
   138	
   139	Keep diagnostic logs to request ID, operation, duration, result count, and error category. Exclude the bundle, refresh and access tokens, query text, node bodies, and provider payloads. A local MCP's logs stay on the user's machine. The API's redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. No read-history UI or auditing subsystem is added. Documentation includes the install and setup flow, private bundle handling, search coverage/limits, sync-gap errors, and source-link limitations.
   140	
   141	## Risks / Trade-offs
   142	
   143	- [Revocation waits for token expiry] → Accepted under A2 (Decision 4). A signed-out session keeps its current access token for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
   144	- [The access token hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup in `mcp_session`, return claims unchanged for other sessions, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook enabled.
   145	- [A read grant missing from `mcp_reader` breaks retrieval silently] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows when the role lacks a grant or a `TO authenticated` policy excludes it. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`, not as `authenticated`.
   146	- [The bundle reads everything the space can read, from a plain file the agent harness can read] → Agent clients keep MCP configuration in plain files on the user's machine (for example `claude_desktop_config.json`, or `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code). Accepted for v0. Setup documentation states the risk.
   147	- [The API carries a bearer token through the website] → An MCP session's token is read-only. A plugin session's token can write, but the API exposes only reads and never stores the token. Redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. A token that leaks stays valid until it expires, up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
   148	- [Cutting off one MCP depends on `mcp-session-access` sign-out] → If per-session sign-out is not in v0 (open there as task 0.4), the only cut-off is changing the space password, which signs out every plugin instance of the space.

51	    10	## What Changes
52	    11	
53	    12	- Provide four read-only operations through both interfaces: get a node, search nodes, discover node types, and get discourse context. The MCP is local: users install it, and the agent client launches it on their machine. Validate setup and these operations in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is not supported in v0.
54	    13	- The plugin hands the agent its own session for the space account, as specified in `mcp-session-access`. The agent acts as the space (Option A2): the session keeps the space account's read access, and the database refuses writes made with it. The MCP's tools and the API's operations also expose only retrieval.
55	    14	- Retrieve every synced discourse node readable by the space account, including accessible shared nodes that have never been imported into the client. Permissions follow current access: new access becomes available and removed access stops working. Signing out a handed-over session stops it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds stay valid until they expire.
56	    15	- Use per-space sessions as the v0 identity model. Access to another space's synced but unpublished nodes requires a bundle from that space. This does not promise one credential representing a person's combined access across spaces.

58	    17	- Reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. V0 does not require title-only re-embedding. 100	     6	## Context
101	     7	
102	     8	See proposal.md for motivation and the four capability specs for the behavior contract. This design follows the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity (see Decision 4). It depends on the `mcp-session-access` handoff specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`, which is not yet in this repository.
103	     9	
104	    10	The checkout has useful pieces, but no implemented agent-grant layer was found:
105	    11	
106	    12	- Both client admin panels create a 45-second handoff through `create_secret_token` and open `/auth/token` with `/auth/group` as the destination. The website establishes a cookie session. `secret_tokens.sql` supports one-time consumption.
107	    13	- `Concept` represents node instances, schemas, and materialized relationships. `Content` joins by `(space_id, source_local_id)` and has multiple variants. The `my_*` views and access helpers already express space and resource-level readability.
108	    14	- `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimensional `text-embedding-3-small` vectors and ranks by cosine distance. Its existing general search RPC has a relevance threshold and no discourse-type predicate. The Roam search experiment subsequently looks up titles and filters locally; that cannot serve headless retrieval.
109	    15	- Obsidian embeds `direct` title content. Roam also embeds `direct_and_description` for some nodes. Preserve these existing vectors and inputs, as agreed; no title-only re-embedding migration is required.
110	    16	- Full content is synced separately. Roam converts it into a cross-app representation; Obsidian stores markdown. Missing full content and missing embeddings are distinct states.
111	    17	- `apps/website/app/api/embeddings/openai/small/route.ts` embeds text with the team's OpenAI key. It has no authentication: it applies CORS only, which non-browser callers ignore.
112	    18	- On `origin/main` (2026-11-11), ENG-1985 added `dbNodeToCrossApp` and `dbNodesToCrossApp`, and ENG-2091 made discovery return `DbCrossAppNode` in a `SharedNodeListing`. The other facts in this list were read from an older checkout of `main`.
113	    19	- Most row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role; four target `authenticated`. No custom access token hook is configured (it is commented out in `packages/database/supabase/config.toml`).
114	    20	
115	    21	## Goals / Non-Goals
116	    22	
117	    23	**Goals:** Reuse existing data, vectors, and access semantics; expose only read operations to agents; keep the MCP and the direct API on the same retrieval semantics; expose sync gaps without silently substituting incomplete content.
118	    24	
119	    25	**Non-Goals:** A new personal identity system, copied permission snapshots, a second embedding pipeline, hybrid ranking, attachment/storage APIs, or a general-purpose database proxy. A separate agent principal (Option B) and a hosted MCP are out of v0. The database package owns SQL/contracts; the website owns the API routes and the local MCP owns its transport.
120	    26	
121	    27	## Decisions
122	    28	
123	    29	### 1. A local MCP that calls the database directly
124	    30	
125	    31	The MCP is a local stdio server that the user installs and the agent client launches on the user's machine. It connects to Supabase with the handed-over space account session and calls the narrow retrieval RPCs directly. No DG-hosted layer sits between the MCP and the database, and no DG-hosted MCP endpoint exists in v0.
126	    32	
127	    33	```
128	    34	Roam / Obsidian --> connect command --> session bundle (shown once)
129	    35	                                               |
130	    36	                                 local MCP config on the user's machine
131	    37	                                               |
132	    38	agent client --stdio--> local MCP --+--> Supabase retrieval RPCs (as the space account)
133	    39	                                    |
134	    40	                                    +--> website embedding route (search queries only)
135	    41	
136	    42	developer --HTTPS + bearer token--> apps/website API routes --> same retrieval RPCs
137	    43	```
138	    44	
139	    45	The retrieval RPCs are the shared core. Each MCP tool validates its inputs, calls one RPC, and returns structured results plus a compact text representation. All tools are marked read-only.
140	    46	
141	    47	The RPCs are a contract with every installed copy of the MCP, and those copies cannot be force-updated. Change an RPC's signature only by adding a new version alongside the old one.
142	    48	
143	    49	**Direct API.** A developer-facing API for callers not using MCP is a set of thin routes in `apps/website` (`headless-retrieval-api`). Each route authenticates the caller's bearer access token against Supabase, embeds search queries on the server, and calls the same retrieval RPCs as the space account, so row-level security applies. The routes hold no credential between requests. The MCP does not depend on them.
144	    50	
145	    51	**Alternative for the API:** documenting the retrieval RPCs themselves as the API needs no hosting, but makes the database schema a public contract, returns raw Postgres errors, and leaves callers to embed queries through the unauthenticated route.
146	    52	
147	    53	**Alternatives:** A hosted remote MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 design) reaches ChatGPT and needs no install, but requires a hosted credential transport. It was rejected on 2026-11-10 in favour of a local MCP, given the constraint to write to the platform later and target users who already work in agentic harnesses. Routing the local MCP through a hosted API was also considered: it would absorb RPC changes, but adds no security, because the database already refuses writes made with the MCP's session (Decision 4).
148	    54	
149	    55	### 2. Hand the MCP its own space account session
150	    56	
151	    57	The credential is a Supabase session for the space account, opened by the plugin and handed over as a bundle: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and refresh token. `mcp-session-access` specifies the handoff, the session registry, and sign-out. The plugin keeps no copy and shows the bundle once. The MCP persists each rotated refresh token and runs as a single instance per bundle. The session's registry row is what makes it read-only (Decision 4).
152	    58	
153	    59	**Alternative (superseded 2026-11-10):** The 2026-09-25 design provisioned a separate Supabase auth user per agent grant, issued an opaque final credential through a website management session, and stored the agent's login secret server-side. That needs a hosted server and a separate principal, and A2 has neither.
154	    60	
155	    61	### 3. ~~Proposed MCP connection uses a credential-bearing URL~~ — removed
156	    62	
157	    63	Removed 2026-11-10. It existed to carry a credential to a hosted MCP through clients that cannot send custom headers. A local MCP reads the bundle from its own configuration. The client/redaction release gate and the OAuth alternative are removed with it.
158	    64	
159	    65	### 4. The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions (Option A2)
160	    66	
161	    67	Decided 2026-11-10: the MCP acts as the space account, and the database refuses writes made with its session. `mcp-session-access` records each handed-over session in `mcp_session`. A Supabase custom access token hook runs whenever a token is issued or refreshed. When the token's session is in `mcp_session`, the hook sets the JWT `role` claim to a read-only database role, `mcp_reader` (name proposed), instead of `authenticated`. Plugin sessions keep `authenticated`.
162	    68	
163	    69	`mcp_reader` has `SELECT` on the tables retrieval reads, and `EXECUTE` on the retrieval RPCs and the access helpers they call. It has no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, and no `EXECUTE` on sync, upsert or `create_secret_token`. Row-level security still applies: policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, and the four `TO authenticated` policies need review. Reads therefore follow the space account's current access with no grant layer.
164	    70	
165	    71	The MCP's tools and the API's operations still expose only retrieval, but they are no longer what enforces read-only.
166	    72	
167	    73	**Revocation is delayed.** The hook runs at issue and refresh, so a signed-out session keeps its current access token until `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this over B's immediate revocation.
168	    74	
169	    75	**Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product notes record "option A2" (Roam block `guIcK3Z9M`) and name the threat as overeager agentic harnesses that bypass the MCP's guards. A tool-layer gate is that kind of guard; a database role is not. The spec owner chose plain A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording.
170	    76	
171	    77	**Alternatives:** (A) the same session with the space account's full permissions and read-only only at the tool layer. It is about a week less work, but any process holding the bundle can write to the space. (B) a separate, permanently read-only agent principal with an `agent_reader` role and a grant table, the 2026-09-25 version of this decision. It revokes immediately, but the 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for about twice A2's extra work.
172	    78	
173	    79	### 5. Represent nodes as CrossApp nodes
174	    80	
175	    81	**Changed 2026-11-13: the node identifier is now the node's `rid`, not `Concept.id`, to match Sid's `shared-node-discovery` spec ([PR #1570](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1570)), in which discovery returns each node as a `CrossAppNode`.** ENG-1985 and ENG-2091 implemented that on 2026-11-11: `dbNodesToCrossApp` in `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts database rows to `DbCrossAppNode` (a `CrossAppNode` with `rid` and `modifiedAt` required), and discovery returns a `SharedNodeListing` of `{ nodes, spaces }`. Retrieval uses the same converter, so an agent and the plugins see the same node under the same ID.
176	    82	
177	    83	**IDs.** A node's ID is its `rid`: its space's URI followed by its `localId` (a Roam block uid, an Obsidian file's ID). A type's ID is the node's `nodeType`: the type's `localId` within the node's space, or the type's `rid` when it belongs to another space. Identically named types in different spaces stay separate. Look a node up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
178	    84	
179	    85	**Payload.** Return each node as a `DbCrossAppNode`, inside an envelope that follows discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` pattern: the spaces map gives each node's space name, URI and platform, and type labels come from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`. Search adds a score and an excerpt per node. Do not define a separate node type for agents.
180	    86	
181	    87	**Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`; `coreTitle` is the title without the type's format. The converter leaves out `content.full`, as discovery does, so get-node fetches the full Content separately, as node import does, and returns stored text/markdown, not rendered HTML. Preserve source links as text; do not fetch referenced assets or mint storage download URLs. Provenance comes from the `rid` and the spaces map. A source link refers to the origin and never claims the node exists in the caller's vault.
182	    88	
183	    89	**Gaps are errors.** `dbNodesToCrossApp` skips any row it cannot convert (missing direct content, author or node type) and logs a warning. Listings and search may skip such rows, as discovery does. Get-node for one ID must not: it converts the row with `dbNodeToCrossApp` and maps the failure to an explicit code, so a node that doesn't exist or isn't readable returns `not_found` and a node lacking its full Content returns `content_unavailable`. Distinguish a stored empty body from a missing row. Fixture validation must exercise these states for both platforms before release.
184	    90	
185	    91	**Type discovery** derives distinct types from readable node instances, independently of embeddings, with labels from the readable schemas. Missing schema data is a sync/access-integrity error, not a reason to bypass permissions.
186	    92	
187	    93	**Alternatives:** `Concept.id` serialized as a decimal string (the previous version of this decision) is a database-internal ID that no plugin uses; it would give the same node a second identity. An agent-specific node payload would rebuild, from the same rows, the second node representation that ENG-2091 just removed. Content IDs as node IDs would expose content variants as duplicate nodes.
188	    94	
189	    95	### 6. Reuse semantic vectors with a retrieval-specific query
190	    96	
191	    97	Embed each search query with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions to match the existing table. A local MCP has no server and no provider key, so it embeds through the existing website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small` and passes the vector to the search RPC. That route is unauthenticated today; see Risks. The API's search route embeds on the server after authenticating the caller. A caller-supplied vector cannot widen access, because the RPC ranks only nodes readable by the caller.
192	    98	
193	    99	Add a dedicated read-only search RPC using the existing embedding table and cosine-distance ordering. Keep existing RPC behavior for current consumers. In this query:
194	   100	
195	   101	- Resolve readable discourse node instances and any selected schema IDs.
196	   102	- Join their current non-obsolete, usable embeddings for existing `direct` and `direct_and_description` content. Preserve the stored input semantics, including descriptions.
197	   103	- Where multiple eligible embeddings represent one node, use its best similarity and return it once.
198	   104	- Sort by similarity descending and node ID as a stable tie-breaker, then apply the requested limit. Authorization, type filtering, and deduplication occur before the limit.
199	   105	
200	   106	Do not copy the current threshold predicate or the Roam experiment's post-limit local filtering. Do not replace the threshold with zero, since negative similarities remain eligible. Do not add keyword indexes, hybrid fusion, or collection re-embedding.
201	   107	
202	   108	Nodes without a current usable embedding are absent from search but remain eligible for get-node/type discovery/context. Embedding-provider failures are errors, not empty results. Create excerpts from the first 300 Unicode code points of available synced body text, with a fallback to the stored semantic input when full content is absent; excerpts are not evidence that the query matched the body. Both interfaces document this behavior.
203	   109	
204	   110	**Alternative:** Calling the existing threshold RPC unchanged violates the agreed no-cutoff behavior and can lose results when type filtering follows its limit. A dedicated query reuses the existing search mechanism while preserving current consumers.
205	   111	
206	   112	### 7. Resolve discourse context using named roles
207	   113	
208	   114	Find readable materialized relation instances connected to the requested node, explicitly filtering `is_relation` and excluding schemas. Use `reference_content` source/destination roles to determine direction; the derived `refs` array identifies candidates but does not encode direction and can include other references. Require the relation, relationship type metadata, and both endpoints to be readable before returning a relationship summary.
209	   115	
210	   116	Return each relation ID with its type, direction, and connected-node summary. Preserve separate materialized relationships rather than deduplicating by labels. A self-link can produce both incoming and outgoing entries. Do not traverse beyond the requested node's incident relationships or expand ordinary backlinks.
211	   117	
212	   118	Return complete one-hop results within the host's response budget. If the result cannot fit, return an explicit `result_too_large` error rather than silently truncate or add an undocumented pagination contract. Full node bodies use the same complete-or-error policy. A proposed 1 MiB serialized response budget is an implementation guardrail to validate against Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, not a relevance or latency target.
213	   119	
214	   120	**Alternative:** Expanding every ID in `refs` would expose non-discourse references and lose direction. Silent truncation would make incomplete discourse context appear complete.
215	   121	
216	   122	### 8. API contract and operational behavior
217	   123	
218	   124	Direct API routes and the corresponding MCP tools:
219	   125	
220	   126	| Direct API | MCP tool | Inputs |
221	   127	| --- | --- | --- |
222	   128	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | Node `rid` |
223	   129	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | Query, optional type IDs, optional limit |
224	   130	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | None |
225	   131	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | Node `rid` |

228	   134	
229	   135	Use shared Zod input/output schemas and generate or check the tool and API documentation against them. 232	   138

235	   141	## Risks / Trade-offs
236	   142	
237	   143	- [Revocation waits for token expiry] → Accepted under A2 (Decision 4). A signed-out session keeps its current access token for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
238	   144	- [The access token hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup in `mcp_session`, return claims unchanged for other sessions, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook enabled.
239	   145	- [A read grant missing from `mcp_reader` breaks retrieval silently] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows when the role lacks a grant or a `TO authenticated` policy excludes it. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`, not as `authenticated`.
240	   146	- [The bundle reads everything the space can read, from a plain file the agent harness can read] → Agent clients keep MCP configuration in plain files on the user's machine (for example `claude_desktop_config.json`, or `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code). Accepted for v0. Setup documentation states the risk.
241	   147	- [The API carries a bearer token through the website] → An MCP session's token is read-only. A plugin session's token can write, but the API exposes only reads and never stores the token. I reviewed `openspec/changes/headless-mcp-retrieval/` and checked its claims against `origin/main`. Your local `main` is 35 commits behind, and the CrossApp converter only exists on `origin/main`.

**Verdict:** most of the codebase facts are accurate. There is one real security gap in A2. The direct API is the main source of extra complexity. The docs could be about 30–40% shorter, mostly by removing change history and repeated text.

## 1. Correctness

**The spec breaks A2's read-only promise.**
- Functions in `public` get `EXECUTE` for `PUBLIC` by default, and no schema file revokes it.
- `create_secret_token` ([secret_tokens.sql:11](packages/database/supabase/schemas/secret_tokens.sql:11)) and `accept_group_invitation` ([account.sql:486](packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql:486)) are `SECURITY DEFINER`. That means `mcp_reader` could call them, and they'd bypass the role's missing table grants.
- Decision 4 says "no EXECUTE on sync, upsert or `create_secret_token`". That's a denylist the current schema doesn't give you.
- The design needs `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC` on write functions, or explicit grants for each function.
- Task 1.3 should list every function `mcp_reader` can execute and compare it to an allowlist, not spot-check three writes.

**Other factual fixes:**
- **"Four `TO authenticated` policies need review":** all four are `storage.objects` policies for the assets bucket, which retrieval never reads. The review item can go. What's actually missing: `mcp_reader` has no table grants (grants go only to `authenticated`/`service_role`), and it needs `GRANT mcp_reader TO authenticator` so PostgREST can switch to it. The spec mentions neither.
- **`rid` format:** Decision 5 says the space URI is followed by the `localId`. That's only true for `http` space URIs. Other spaces get an `orn:<platform>.<subtype>:…/<localId>` form ([rid.ts:10-23](packages/database/src/lib/rid.ts)).
- **45-second handoff:** the 45s is set by the Roam and Obsidian admin panels. `create_secret_token` defaults to 30 days.
- **Conversion failures:** `dbNodeToCrossApp` also throws when the local id, space or created date is missing, not just the three cases listed. Get-node's error mapping has to cover those too.
- **"Read from an older checkout" caveat (design line 18):** I checked the claims against `origin/main` and they hold, so the caveat can go.

**The spec contradicts itself:**
- **Limit above 30:** the spec scenario says the service caps it at 30. Decision 8 says it's rejected with `invalid_request`. Pick one; I'd keep the rejection.
- **Signed-out sessions:** the requirement "signed-out sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval" conflicts with "access tokens MAY remain valid until expiry". Change the first to "missing or expired".
- **Which sessions the API accepts:** the parity requirement says the MCP and the API accept "the same handed-over session". Risks line 147 says the API also accepts plugin sessions, which can write.

## 2. Simplicity

- **Cut the direct API (group 5) from v0.** It adds hosting, a bearer-auth helper, HTTP error mapping, log redaction across hosting and proxy layers, docs and parity tests (6.1). The stated reason for it, that documenting the RPCs makes the schema a public contract, is weak: Decision 1 already makes the RPCs a pinned contract with every installed MCP copy. The "Why" is about agent clients, and a developer can call the RPCs with the bundle exactly as the MCP does. This roughly halves groups 5 and 6.
- **The 1 MiB budget and `result_too_large`:** one-hop context returns summaries only, so it's unlikely to hit 1 MiB. Keep it for get-node bodies only, or defer it.
- **Shared Zod schemas that generate or check the docs:** fine if they're cheap, but this is extra work with only one interface.

## 3. Gaps

- **Type IDs are ambiguous across spaces.** Discovery returns types from several spaces. A local-id `nodeType` only makes sense relative to its own space, so a search filter of `["abc"]` doesn't say which space it means. Use type `rid`s everywhere in the agent contract.
- **Refresh-token storage.** The bundle sits in the client's config file. After the first refresh that copy is stale, so the MCP needs its own state file. The spec should say where that file lives, and that recovering from a lost file means getting a new bundle.
- **One instance per bundle means one bundle per client.** A user running Claude Desktop and Claude Code needs two bundles. The setup docs should say so.
- **Embedding route hardening.** The MCP depends on the unauthenticated route. To make adding auth later non-breaking, have the MCP send the access token now, even though the route ignores it.
- **Packaging and versioning.** The spec doesn't cover how the MCP is distributed (npm or `npx`), how a client finds out it needs an update, or a minimum RPC version check. Codex config is TOML, so the setup docs differ by client.

## 4. Verbosity (cut list)

- **Remove the change history.** This covers the date stamps in the HTML comments, the "spec owner chose A on 11-12, then A2 on 11-13" passage (duplicated in proposal line 48 and design line 75), the Decision 3 tombstone, the superseded alternative in Decision 2, the bold "Changed 2026-11-13" in Decision 5, and the "Historical July aspirations" line. Git and Linear keep the history.
- **Say each repeated point once.**
  - The delayed-revocation caveat appears 6 times.
  - The multi-space open question appears 5 times.
  - The unauthenticated embedding route appears 4 times.
  - RPC versioning appears twice.
- **Shrink the proposal's "What Changes".** It restates the spec requirements nearly line for line. Keep the why, the capability list and the boundaries.
- **Delete the "Per-capability open decisions" section in design.md.** Everything in it except the multi-space question just says it's covered elsewhere.
- **Fold `README.md` into the proposal**, since it adds nothing.

## What's going on To search, the MCP turns the user's query into a vector by calling the website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small`. That route uses **our** OpenAI key and **checks nothing**: anyone who knows the URL can call it and spend our quota. We'll want to lock it down eventually. The problem is timing. ## Why "later" is a trap Once someone installs the MCP, that copy stays on their machine. We can't force-update it. Say v0 ships an MCP that calls the route with no token, and later we add a check that rejects calls without one: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant MCP as Installed MCP (v0, no token) participant Route as Embedding route (hardened later) MCP->>Route: embed "my query" (no token) Route-->>MCP: 401 rejected Note over MCP: Search is broken for every
user who hasn't updated ``` So hardening the route would break search for every existing install. That's already the situation with the shipped Roam and Obsidian plugins, and it's why the spec calls hardening a follow-up. ## The fix: send the token now, ignore it for now The MCP already holds an access token, since it uses one for the database. Have it attach that token to embedding calls from day one, even though the route doesn't check it yet. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Today A[MCP v0
sends token] -->|token ignored| R1[Route: no check] end subgraph Later B[Same MCP v0
sends token] -->|token verified ✅| R2[Route: checks token] C[Random caller
no token] -->|rejected ❌| R2 end ``` When we later turn on the check: - Every installed MCP already sends a valid token, so nothing breaks. - Callers with no token get rejected, which is the point. ## Cost vs payoff - **Cost now:** one extra header (`Authorization: Bearer `) on one fetch call. - **Payoff later:** the route can be locked down without breaking installed MCPs. Of the three kinds of caller, only the Roam and Obsidian plugins would still need a migration plan. It's like adding a door key slot before installing the lock: everyone who's already holding a key walks in fine on the day the lock goes on.
